## Give ourselves a Hessian

![](Figures/fig3-hessian-peaks.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

::: {.notes}
~40 s. Just give ourselves a Hessian. Curvature at the top = precision of the normal. Land on the flat peak: it's an approximation. Bridge: many numbers → the curvature is a grid, and that grid is a precision matrix like the last slide.
:::

~80 s, two clicks. Diagonal → click → block diagonal → click → block and banded (yours): modelling data-level dependence is hard.
:::
